definitions: To start to happen or work.
To encourage someone to do something, especially to hurry or try harder.
To appear on stage, television, or radio.
To begin to feel an illness or a mood.
To try to attract someone sexually.
To be broadcast or shown (of a programme, film, etc.).
examples: You've really come on with your English.
Come on, we're going to be late!
The band came on at 9 pm.
I feel a cold coming on.
He was really coming on to her at the party.
What time does the news come on?
